```{r setup}
#| include: false
if (nzchar(params$pkg_path) && dir.exists(file.path(params$pkg_path, "R"))) {
  devtools::load_all(params$pkg_path, quiet = TRUE)
} else {
  library(stateELP)
}

spec <- read_el_spec(params$spec_file)

# Dev mode by default: the document runs the stage. `results_file` switches to
# RDS mode, which is how the Decision stage will read what earlier stages
# produced. Analysis logic lives in R/, never here: this file holds the prose,
# the captions, and one call per figure or table.
res <- if (!is.null(params$results_file) && nzchar(params$results_file)) {
  readRDS(params$results_file)
} else {
  # The roster carries the cohort and its characteristics; the academic table
  # is what the achievement comparison needs.
  bundle <- as_el_data(el_long_sim, roster = el_roster_sim,
                       academic = academic_long_sim, spec = spec)
  run_check2(bundle, spec)
}

# Which slots came back. `h` is "has it", `n` is "is it missing": Quarto reads a
# second `!` inside `!expr` as a second YAML tag, so the negation is its own
# name.
slots <- c("crosstab", "academic_summary", "trajectories", "blocked_groups")
h <- vapply(slots, function(s) !is.null(res[[s]]), TRUE)
n <- !h

min_cell <- spec_min_cell(spec)
panel_last <- res$meta$panel[[2]]
component <- spec_headline_label(spec)

# Only when this state's on-time deadline is keyed by starting band, which
# makes the Initial ELP block a comparison against different clocks.
have_band_clock <- !is.na(res$meta$band_clock_note)

# Captions are built here, not inline in a chunk header: a colon-space inside
# an `!expr` value is read as a YAML mapping and the render fails.
crosstab_cap <- if (h[["crosstab"]]) {
  paste(
    sprintf("Exit outcomes and the characteristics of each group, %s cohort, observed through %d.",
            res$meta$cohort, panel_last),
    # Kept on one line: a test greps this document for the phrase, and a
    # sprintf split across source lines would hide it.
    sprintf("Every indicator is relative to the years observed, so No_Exit means not observed exiting by %d, not never exiting.",
            panel_last),
    "Blocks below the first two rows are column percentages.",
    sprintf("Cells under %d are suppressed.", min_cell))
} else {
  "Exit outcomes"
}

academic_cap <- if (h[["academic_summary"]]) {
  sprintf(paste0("%s achievement by exit group at the same year in status, %s ",
                 "cohort. The grade beside each year is the modal grade of the ",
                 "students in it."),
          res$meta$academic_subject, res$meta$cohort)
} else {
  "Academic achievement by exit group"
}

academic_fig_cap <- if (h[["academic_summary"]]) {
  sprintf(paste0("Share at or above the %s proficiency cut, by exit group and ",
                 "year in status. A group with nobody left to measure has no ",
                 "point rather than a zero."),
          res$meta$academic_subject)
} else {
  "Academic proficiency by exit group"
}

traj_fig_cap <- if (h[["trajectories"]]) {
  sprintf(paste0("Mean %s level by year in status, drawn separately for each ",
                 "exit group. There is deliberately no pooled cohort line: see ",
                 "the caution below. Lines stop where a group no longer has ",
                 "students being assessed."),
          component)
} else {
  "ELP level by year in status"
}
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="default" icon=false}
## Sample

`r res$meta$sample`
:::

## Looking at

A comparison of two groups from the Data Check 1 cohort --- students who exited
on time, and students whose EL classification was prolonged --- across
demographic and program characteristics: home language, district size, sex,
socioeconomic status, disability status, the type of EL services received, and
the ELP band a student started in. Alongside it, a descriptive summary of
academic achievement at comparable points in each group's trajectory, and the
ELP levels each group posted on the way there.

The groups are defined against the years actually observed, and all three exit
indicators are relative to that window:

- **On time** (`Exit_OnTime`) --- first observed as a former EL within
  `r res$meta$on_time_text` of entering status, which is this state's
  ESSA-expected timeline
  `r if (isTRUE(res$meta$on_time_provisional)) "[DERIVED --- VERIFY]" else ""`
- **Prolonged** --- everyone still in view who did not exit on time: students
  who exited after that timeline, and students never observed to exit
  (`No_Exit`).
- **Disappeared** --- last seen before the window closed, with no exit
  observed. Their outcome is unknown, so they are a column of their own and
  are never counted as on time or as prolonged.

`Exit_Ever`, `Exit_Max` and `Exit_OnTime` are nested --- every on-time exiter
is also a maximum-timeline exiter and an ever-exiter --- so those three columns
do not add up. What adds up is `Exit_Ever` + `No_Exit` + `Disappeared` = All.

## Looking for

Two things.

1. **Whether prolonged classification goes with specific, identifiable
   characteristics.** Disability status, mobility, home language, particular
   districts or programs. A characteristic that is over-represented among
   prolonged students is a candidate explanation for why they are still
   classified; one that is spread evenly across both groups is not.
2. **Whether the on-time group already looks academically stronger, even at
   similar ELP levels.** If it does, something other than English proficiency
   may be separating the two groups. This is the descriptive companion to the
   formal test in Data Check 1.

## The cohort, split by exit outcome

```{r}
#| label: tbl-crosstab
#| tbl-cap: !expr crosstab_cap
#| eval: !expr h[["crosstab"]]
ft_check2_crosstab(res)
```

```{r}
#| output: asis
#| eval: !expr n[["crosstab"]]
cat("> **No crosstab.** ", res$meta$note, "\n", sep = "")
```

```{r}
#| output: asis
#| eval: !expr have_band_clock
cat("::: {.callout-warning appearance=\"default\" icon=false}\n",
    "## Reading the Initial ELP block\n\n",
    res$meta$band_clock_note, "\n:::\n", sep = "")
```

The first two rows are the balance of the cohort across exit outcomes. Every
block below them is a set of column percentages: read down a block within one
column to see what that group is made of, and across a row to see how the
groups differ.

The first two blocks are read differently from the third. Home language,
district size, service type and initial ELP band **partition** each column, so
their percentages sum to 100% --- a category for students whose value was not
reported keeps that true, rather than quietly shrinking the denominator. The
"other demographics" rows are **independent shares** of each column and sum to
nothing: a student can be counted in all three or none. Where a value is not
reported, that student leaves the row's denominator instead of being counted as
a "no". An exit outcome that no student in this cohort landed in has nobody to
describe, so its block cells are blank rather than zero --- its count in the
first row is what tells you the column is empty.

```{r}
#| output: asis
#| eval: !expr h[["crosstab"]]
cat("Characteristics are read **at entry** --- the cohort's own start year, the one year every member is current by construction --- so a block describes who these students were when they entered, not something that moved with them. Two are derived rather than delivered: district size is the entry-year district banded by that district's own EL count, and the initial ELP band is the first annual ", component, " level, taken from the same derivation Data Check 1's band-split curve uses so the two stages cannot disagree.\n", sep = "")
```


```{r}
#| label: fig-academic
#| fig-cap: !expr academic_fig_cap

plot_academic_summary(res$academic_summary, spec)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-academic
#| tbl-cap: !expr academic_cap
#| eval: !expr h[["academic_summary"]]
ft_check2_academic(res)
```

Comparing the groups at the same **year in status** rather than in the same
calendar year is what makes this readable: two students four years into EL
status are at the same point in their own trajectories, whoever they are. For a
cohort that all entered in the same grade, each year in status is mostly a
single grade, which is why the proficiency rate can be read down the column at
all; the modal grade is printed beside each year so that assumption stays
visible rather than implied.

## ELP trajectories, by exit group

```{r}
#| label: fig-trajectories

plot_trajectories(res$trajectories$levels, spec)
```

::: {.callout-important appearance="default" icon=false}
## Caution: do not mistake group change for achievement trajectories

It is not necessarily that the same students are growing less over time. It is
also that the slowest growers are the ones who stay.

A single cohort-average ELP line over time falls for both reasons at once and
cannot separate them, so this document does not draw one. The table below is
the mechanism: it shows who is still being assessed each year. As the on-time
group exits it stops contributing scores, and the average of whoever is left
drifts down without any individual student having slowed.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-composition
#| tbl-cap: "Share of the students still being assessed each year in status, by exit group. This is why a pooled cohort average would mislead."
#| eval: !expr h[["trajectories"]]
ft_check2_composition(res)
```

```{r}
#| output: asis
#| eval: !expr n[["trajectories"]]
cat("Trajectories not shown: no annual ", component, " level resolves for this cohort, or the level scale is categorical and has no mean.\n", sep = "")
```

## Interpreting it

This is the descriptive companion to Data Check 1's formal test. Data Check 1
asks whether exit timing is being driven by English proficiency as intended;
this check puts a human face on who the "stuck" population is. That matters for
what an eventual recommendation should include. If disability status is a major
driver of prolonged classification, for example, a threshold change alone will
not address the underlying issue: it would move some students, and leave the
students held back by something other than their English exactly where they
were.

::: {.callout-important appearance="default" icon=false}
## Reminder: this is not automatically about the cut score

The first two data views are about the interactions between policies,
programs, population, and exit criteria. The response to findings here is not
necessarily to change your cut score.
:::

Three more cautions carry the weight here.

**Read a difference between the groups as a description, not a cause.** A
characteristic that is more common among prolonged students says who the stuck
population is. It does not say why they are stuck, and two characteristics that
travel together (district size and type of instructional model, say) cannot be
told apart in a crosstab. Separating them needs a model that holds the others
constant, which is a later addition and not in this document.

**Some of the academic gap is definitional.** On-time exiters left because they
cleared an English proficiency bar, and the content assessment is taken in
English, so finding them academically stronger is partly built into how the two
groups were defined. The question worth asking of the table above is whether
the gap is *larger* than that explains, and whether it is still there at
similar ELP levels --- which is what the trajectory figure lets you check.

**`No_Exit` is "not observed exiting", and the window is finite.** The
`r res$meta$cohort` cohort is followed through `r panel_last`. A student
counted as `No_Exit` was still classified at the window's edge; nothing here
says they will never exit. Likewise, `Exit_OnTime` and `Exit_Max` are counted
against the years available, and a caption has to say so.

::: {.callout-important appearance="default" icon=false}
## Caution: remember your data structure

This cohort is students who started in `r res$meta$start_grade`. It is the best
case for exit: later entrants, including newcomers arriving in the upper
grades, are not in this table at all. Read it as the make-up of one entry
cohort, never as the state's overall exit picture.
:::

## Additional check --- Types 2--6: blocked by one criterion only

```{r}
#| output: asis
#| eval: !expr n[["blocked_groups"]]
cat(res$meta$blocked_note, "\n")
```

When it applies, the groups Prep Step 2 identified as blocked by one criterion
only are added as further comparison groups alongside the on-time and prolonged
exiters. A group that looks systematically different --- demographically,
academically, in program experience --- means that criterion is screening on
something other than what the main score screens on.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-blocked
#| tbl-cap: "Students blocked by exactly one exit criterion, as a share of each exit outcome. A student blocked by different criteria in different years is counted under the one that blocked them most often."
#| eval: !expr h[["blocked_groups"]]
ft_check2_blocked_groups(res)
```

## Still to come

The deck's further views for this data check are recorded and not built:
repeating the analysis for students who start in later grades, and adding
starting grade as its own set of crosstab rows, to see whether entry grade
predicts which group a student lands in; and a statistical model --- logistic
regression --- to control for the correlations among characteristics that the
crosstab can only show one at a time. Each is a later addition.

## Decide before moving on

- **Do specific subgroups warrant separate treatment in Data Checks 3--4?**
  A group that is heavily over-represented among prolonged students may need
  its own analysis there, rather than being averaged into the whole.
- **What equity considerations does the final recommendation need to address
  explicitly?** In particular, whether any characteristic that separates the
  prolonged group is one a change to the threshold would leave untouched.
:::
